148.canonical: Design Stage 2 backward from the evidence needed rather than from learner interest: a fun, complex, or beloved project can sample only a small slice of the standard and bypass its core demand, while a less engaging exercise can yield more conclusive evidence — confusing an interesting activity with a valid assessment is the common error.

161.canonical: Self-test every assessment in both directions — how likely a student could score well without demonstrating the understanding sought (by guessing, parroting, effort, lovely products, or articulateness), and how likely a student could score poorly despite significant understanding (because the task is irrelevant or the criteria arbitrary) — and treat anything other than very unlikely on either as meaning the evidence is probably not valid.

163.canonical: Address the two distinct reliability problems in performance assessment separately — generalizing from too few performances (a result may reflect an untypical day rather than a pattern) and judges scoring the same performance differently — using multiple tasks for the same outcome and well-trained supervised judges working from clear rubrics and specific anchors, accepting that measurement error is unavoidable and can only be minimized to tolerable levels.
